summary.business_type: Publisher / Affiliate Content Site (piano learning reviews & guides)
top_findings: 5 pages have title tags over 60 characters and will truncate in Google's SERP snippet
1 page (/pianoforall-vs-alfreds-piano-book/) is canonicalized to another URL but is still listed in the XML sitemap, sending mixed signals to crawlers
6 pages are missing a meta description, so Google will auto-generate the snippet
26 of 416 images (6%) across 16 pages are missing alt text
5 standard security response headers are absent (X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options, CSP, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy)
quick_wins: Add meta descriptions to the 6 pages missing one (cookie-policy, contact, privacy-policy, acoustic-vs-digital-piano, how-to-tune-a-piano-a-simple-guide, ahmad-jamal-biography)
Trim the 13 titles over 60 characters so they don't truncate in search results
Remove /pianoforall-vs-alfreds-piano-book/ from sitemap-posts.xml since it's canonicalized elsewhere, or merge/de-duplicate the content
Add alt text to the 26 images currently missing it
Add the 5 missing security headers at the CDN/edge (Caddy config visible in response headers)

categories.name: Technical SEO
what_works: robots.txt is clean and correctly references the sitemap; only Ghost admin/system paths are disallowed
XML sitemap index + 4 sub-sitemaps (pages, posts, authors, tags) all resolve and parse correctly
HSTS is enabled (max-age=31536000)
HTTP/2 in use, served via Caddy
All 45 crawled pages returned clean 200s, no 4xx/5xx encountered
No noindex directives found on any content page

findings.title: Sitemap includes a canonicalized-away URL
findings.description: /pianoforall-vs-alfreds-piano-book/ has <link rel="canonical" href="https://pianoers.com/pianoforall-review/"> (it also duplicates that page's title and meta description exactly) but remains listed in sitemap-posts.xml. Sitemaps should only list canonical/indexable URLs.
findings.recommendation: Either remove this URL from the sitemap and rely on the canonical tag, or if it's meant to be a distinct comparison page, give it its own unique title/meta/content and self-canonical it.

findings.title: Standard security headers absent
findings.description: The homepage response (via Caddy) includes strict-transport-security but not X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options, Content-Security-Policy, Referrer-Policy, or Permissions-Policy.
findings.recommendation: Add these headers at the Caddy/CDN edge layer. Low engineering cost, standard hardening.

findings.title: x-powered-by header discloses stack
findings.description: Response includes 'x-powered-by: Express', unnecessarily revealing backend technology.
findings.recommendation: Strip the X-Powered-By header at the edge/proxy layer.

findings.title: HTTP→HTTPS redirect and www subdomain not independently verifiable
findings.description: This audit ran from a sandboxed session whose network egress filters non-proxied plain-HTTP (port 80) requests and returns synthetic responses for unresolved subdomains, so port-80 redirect behavior and any www.pianoers.com configuration could not be reliably tested from this environment. All HTTPS (443) checks above are reliable.
findings.recommendation: Manually verify http://pianoers.com redirects to https://pianoers.com/, and confirm whether www.pianoers.com is intentionally unused or should redirect to the apex domain.

categories.name: Content Quality
what_works: 44 of 45 pages exceed 300 words; the one short page is /contact/ (73 words), which is expected for a contact page

Strong E-E-A-T signal: Article schema includes an author Person object with name, photo, author page URL, and an external sameAs verification link (onlinepianoteachers.com) — genuine third-party authority signal
Author bylines link to /author/{name}/ pages on content posts
dateModified is present and current in schema (e.g. 2026-02-22), indicating active content maintenance

findings.title: Duplicate content between two review pages
findings.description: /pianoforall-vs-alfreds-piano-book/ and /pianoforall-review/ share an identical title and meta description, and the former is canonicalized to the latter — suggesting the comparison page may be thin/duplicate content rather than a distinct resource.
findings.recommendation: Differentiate the comparison page with unique content genuinely comparing the two products, or fold it into the main review as a section.

categories.name: On-Page SEO
what_works: Every page has exactly one H1 except one (see finding below)
Canonical tags present on all pages
Open Graph title/description/image present on all 45 pages

findings.title: 13 titles exceed 60 characters
findings.description: 13 of 45 pages (29%) have title tags longer than 60 characters and will likely truncate in Google's SERP, e.g. 'Best Free Piano Learning Apps: 7 Apps That Actually Work for Beginners' (80 chars), 'Yamaha P-145 / P-145BT Review in 2026: Still My #1 Pick for Beginners' (69 chars).
findings.recommendation: Trim these titles to under ~60 characters while preserving the primary keyword near the front.

findings.title: 6 pages missing meta description
findings.description: cookie-policy, contact, privacy-policy, acoustic-vs-digital-piano, how-to-tune-a-piano-a-simple-guide, and ahmad-jamal-biography have no meta description tag.
findings.recommendation: Write unique 120-160 character descriptions for each, especially the two content pages (acoustic-vs-digital-piano, how-to-tune-a-piano) which are indexable and could otherwise rank.

findings.title: 14 meta descriptions exceed 160 characters
findings.description: 14 pages have descriptions that will truncate in the SERP, up to 224 characters on /pianote-review/.
findings.recommendation: Trim to 150-160 characters, front-loading the value proposition.

findings.title: Duplicate title and meta description pair
findings.description: /pianoforall-review/ and /pianoforall-vs-alfreds-piano-book/ share an identical title ("Piano For All Review: A Pro Pianist's Take (2026)") and meta description.
findings.recommendation: Resolve alongside the canonical/duplicate-content issue above — give the comparison page its own unique title and description if kept as a separate page.

findings.title: Two H1s on privacy-policy page
findings.recommendation: Demote the secondary H1 to an H2, low priority given it's a legal boilerplate page.

categories.name: Schema / Structured Data
what_works: All 45 crawled pages carry valid JSON-LD
Article schema used consistently with publisher, author (Person + image + sameAs), headline, dates, and mainEntityOfPage
Review schema on 6 product review pages, FAQPage on 5 guide pages, ItemList on 2 roundup pages, WebSite schema on the homepage
Author entity includes an external sameAs link, which strengthens E-E-A-T/entity recognition for both traditional and AI search

findings.title: Review schema completeness not fully verified
findings.description: Spot-checked Review schema blocks were present but this audit did not exhaustively validate every Review block against Google's rich-result requirements (itemReviewed, reviewRating with ratingValue/bestRating, author) across all 6 review pages.
findings.recommendation: Run all 6 review pages through Google's Rich Results Test to confirm eligibility for review star rich snippets.

categories.name: Performance (Core Web Vitals)
what_works: Homepage HTML payload is lightweight (~66KB)
Static server-rendered HTML (Ghost/Caddy), no client-side rendering framework or SPA hydration delay
Lazy-loading (loading="lazy") is used on the majority of in-article images (13/20 sampled)

findings.title: No field or lab Core Web Vitals data — estimate only
findings.description: This audit ran without PageSpeed Insights/CrUX API credentials and without a working headless-Chromium pipeline in this sandbox, so LCP/INP/CLS could not be measured directly. The score below is a heuristic estimate based on render-blocking resource count only, not real user or lab timing data.
findings.recommendation: Run scripts/pagespeed_check.py or PageSpeed Insights manually with a Google API key for real LCP/INP/CLS numbers.

findings.title: 5 render-blocking scripts and 2 blocking stylesheets in <head>
findings.description: Homepage <head> loads 5 scripts without async/defer (Ghost portal.min.js, sodo-search.min.js, cards.min.js, comment-counts.min.js, ghost-stats.min.js) plus 2 blocking stylesheets, which can delay First Contentful Paint.
findings.recommendation: Add defer to non-critical scripts (comment-counts, ghost-stats, sodo-search) so they don't block initial render.

findings.title: Homepage thumbnail images not lazy-loaded
findings.description: The 8 card-thumbnail images sampled on the homepage lack loading="lazy", unlike in-article images elsewhere on the site.
findings.recommendation: Add loading="lazy" to below-the-fold homepage thumbnails; leave the first 1-2 above-the-fold images eager.

categories.name: AI Search Readiness (GEO)
what_works: llms.txt is present at /llms.txt and well-structured: it summarizes the site's purpose and links out to homepage, about, and every review/guide by category — uncommon and genuinely useful for AI crawlers/citation systems
robots.txt has no disallow rules targeting GPTBot, ClaudeBot, Google-Extended, PerplexityBot, or CCBot — the site is open to AI crawlers by default
Article schema + verified author entities (sameAs) give LLM systems clear attribution and authority signals for citation
Content is written in a first-person, opinionated review style ("I review its methods...") which tends to perform well for AI-citation passage extraction

findings.title: No explicit AI-crawler allow rules
findings.description: robots.txt uses a blanket 'User-agent: *' with no specific rules for AI bots, which is functionally open but doesn't explicitly signal intent.
findings.recommendation: Optional: add explicit 'User-agent: GPTBot / Allow: /' style entries if you want to make AI-crawler policy unambiguous, though this is not required since the blanket rule already allows them.

categories.name: Images
what_works: One homepage image already uses WebP
In-article images generally use responsive width-suffixed URLs (/size/w720/...)
Most in-article images are lazy-loaded

findings.title: 26 of 416 images (6%) missing alt text across 16 pages
findings.recommendation: Add descriptive alt text to all flagged images; prioritize the 3 pages above.

findings.title: Most sampled images are JPEG/PNG rather than WebP/AVIF
findings.description: Of 8 homepage images sampled, 6 were JPEG, 1 PNG, and only 1 WebP, ranging 33-60KB each.
findings.recommendation: Serve images as WebP/AVIF with JPEG fallback to reduce payload; Ghost supports this via image optimization plugins/CDN transforms.

phases.name: Phase 1: Critical Fixes
items: Resolve the /pianoforall-vs-alfreds-piano-book/ vs /pianoforall-review/ duplicate title/meta/canonical conflict
Add meta descriptions to the 6 pages missing one

phases.name: Phase 2: High-Impact Improvements
items: Trim the 14 meta descriptions over 160 characters
Add the 5 missing security headers (X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options, CSP, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy) at the Caddy edge
Add defer to the 3 non-critical render-blocking scripts (comment-counts, ghost-stats, sodo-search)
Add alt text to the 26 images missing it, starting with the 3 worst-offending pages

phases.name: Phase 3: Content & Authority
items: Run all 6 Review-schema pages through Google's Rich Results Test
Convert remaining JPEG/PNG images to WebP/AVIF
Verify http→https redirect and www subdomain behavior manually (not testable from this sandbox)

phases.name: Phase 4: Monitoring & Iteration
items: Get PageSpeed Insights / CrUX API access set up for real Core Web Vitals field data
Re-run this audit after Phase 1-2 fixes to confirm resolution and re-score

artifacts.note: Screenshots were not captured: Playwright/Chromium visual capture was not exercised in this audit run.
